articles.title: Just 50 Copies of Vampirella's Debut Comic Exist in This Grade or Better, Making This Auction a Rare Opportunity
articles.summary: One of the most iconic creations of the Silver Age not to emerge from Marvel or DC, Vampirella’s 1969 first appearance is today one of the rarest and most sought-after keys of its era. The CGC population report lists only 1,353 graded copies of the comic magazine in existence, only fifty of which are certified […]
articles.content:
While her provocative costume can certainly be credited for some of Vampirella’s lasting appeal, to attribute all of her popularity to the comics’ cheesecake qualities is to do Vampirella a disservice. It also does a disservice to the work of a legion of the medium’s best writers and artists a disservice, including names like Mark Millar, Grant Morrison, and Alan Moore. Vampirella’s earliest years with Warren Publishing are still among the best stories to feature the character. Warren’s Vampirella began as a horror anthology in the tradition of Tales from the Crypt or Warren’s own Eerie and Creepy before evolving into a horror-tinged super-hero comic with Vampirella at its center. However, this came at the cost of lacking the widespread distribution enjoyed by more traditional, kid-friendly comics. As a result, all issues of the Warren Vampirella are scarce, and it’s among the most challenging Bronze Age comic titles to collect a complete run of. No issue is rarer than Vampirella #1, and next week, Heritage is giving collectors the chance to own one of just thirty-five copies CGC-graded at a 9.4 .

Not belonging to one of the “big two” (Marvel and DC), the rights to Vampirella have changed hands several times across her history, first from Warren Publishing to Harris Publications, then from Harris Publications to Dynamite Entertainment. Between these three publishers, Vampirella has been relaunched as an ongoing comics series fifteen times from 1992 to the present. Almost every writer to take on one of these monthly titles has had their own spin to put on her origins, character, and world. As a result, depending on who you ask, Vampirella is an alien from planet Drakulon, the daughter of the Biblical Lilith, a scream queen, a secret monster-hunting agent for the Vatican, and the bride of Dracula. For the past seven years, Christopher Priest has been at the helm of Dynamite’s Vampirella, and has somehow taken all of these disparate elements and made them (mostly) work in one canon.

To begin with, yes, really: Drakulon. Vampirella’s classic comic book origin is absolutely ridiculous, though her real-world origins carry a surprising pedigree. The character is credited, broadly, as emerging from the imagination of Famous Monsters editor Forrest J. Ackerman. Apocryphally, the name came from Ackerman combining “vampire” and Barbarella , the Roger Vadim film adaptation of which was a major cult hit the previous year. Underground comic writer and artist (and later comic book historian) Trina Robbins designed Vampirella’s costume and overall look, some of her first major mainstream work. Tom Sutton illustrated her first appearance, while Frank Frazetta contributed the cover. Ackerman wrote the issue, which introduced Vampirella as an alien from Drakulon, planet of the vampires, where blood flows from great rivers. Faced with a great catastrophe as Drakulon’s rivers dry and its people starve, Vampirella is forced to flee the planet for Earth, hitching a ride aboard a crash-landed space probe. On her journey to Earth, Vampirella discovers that the blood she needs to survive flows in the veins of these alien “humans,” forcing her to kill for sustinence.

Vampirella disappeared to the background of her magazine for its first few years, serving as a hostess to the anthology horror stories within, introducing them like the Crypt-Keeper or DC’s Cain and Abel. Sporadically, she’d get a short feature story. Readers responded well to her stories, and she gradually took over the book. Naturally, this eventually included a confrontation with Dracula, revealed as a member of her own species, the “Vampiri.” Eventually curing herself of her thirst for blood through the Necronomicon-esque book of magic the “Crimson Chronicles,” Vampirella became a force for good and a hunter of monsters, teaming with characters like the sorcerer Pendragon and Adam Van Helsing, descendant of Dracula’s nemesis. The Warren run lasted one hundred and thirteen issues, ending in 1983 when Warren Publishing filed for bankruptcy. Harris Publications bought their assets at auction, this included Vampirella. Harris reprinted the entire Warren run throughout the eighties, finally launching a new Vampirella title in 1991 – naturally coming in the midst of the era’s comic speculation boom.

Kurt Busiek revamped Vampirella’s origins for Harris Publication, introducing the alternate backstory that she is the daughter of Lilith, the first wife of Adam and the “mother of demons” in traditional Judeo-Christian myth. Repentant, Lilith trained her daughter Vampirella to battle the demons she had spawned. Warren Ellis incorporated “Drakulon” back into canon with his Vampirella Lives mini-series, which establishes it as Vampirella’s birthplace and a realm of Hell. Grant Morrison and Mark Millar’s work on the Vampirella ongoing title is considered a high water mark for the Harris era, featuring religious conspiracies, vampire gangsters, and a new nemesis for Vampi with the lich Von Kriest. Characters and continuity from Harris were kept roughly intact for the early Dynamite era, which also reintroduced Warren-era characters like Adam Van Helsing and Pendragon. A reboot reimagined her as an agent of a B.P.R.D-esque monster-hunting organization run by the Vatican; another reboot put her in a dystopian future. For the better part of a decade, Christopher Priest has been trying to make all of these interpretations make sense together.

For the most part, Priest has succeeded: his Vampirella run has been upheld by readers as one of the best iterations of the title, with more complex characterization and intricate storytelling than many of its precursors. That it’s managed to fly under the radar is a reminder that Vampirella remains a cult character, maintaining a dedicated fanbase while never cracking most readers’ pull list. It’s that niche status that enables writers like Priest, Morrison, or Alan Moore (who penned a 1997 Vampirella/ Dracula cross-over) to exercise unrestrained creativity when writing for Vampirella: they aren’t subject to the same pressures and oversight that comes with working on a mainstream title.

Tying together science fiction, horror, and a traditional super-hero comic, Vampirella is a surprisingly versatile character. While the combination of these genres doesn’t work for every reader, for those who it resonates with, it really resonates , making Vampirella an ardent favorite of theirs. It’s those hardcore fans that drive the high aftermarket prices on her classic Warren appearances, with Vampirella #1 seldom selling for less than $500. The copy on auction at Heritage has already attained a price of more than $3k – higher than average for the book in high grade condition, but explicable given its exceptional 9.6 Near-Mint condition. With more than a week left to bid, the price is likely to climb even higher, cementing Vampirella’s status once again as an underrated icon, far more than an outrageous costume and a campy name.

articles.title: One of 2026's Biggest Bombs Might Actually Be A Streaming Hit, Continuing a Big Trend for One Director
articles.summary: In the past several years, it’s clear that the movie industry is shifting dramatically. The introduction of a bunch of new streaming services in the late 2010s and early 2020s has accelerated things, and the COVID-19 pandemic seemingly had a lasting influence on the public’s moviegoing habits. And many thinkpieces later, everyone is just as […]
articles.content:
Certainly, the bar for what films audiences are willing to see in theaters has been raised to some degree. But there isn’t a clear balance between whether moviegoers want more franchise movies or original stories. As soon as industry insiders declare that superhero cinema is less reliable than it once was, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will come out and shatter records. When someone assumes that original films are dead on arrival once they hit theaters, something like Obsession will release and change everything. But one director released two box office disappointments in 2026 and could again be banking on the saving grace of streaming.

Laika — the studio behind stop-motion animated films like Coraline , Paranorman , and Kubo and the Two Strings — had been developing Wildwood for 15 years. The long-discussed project is based on the 2011 novel written by Colin Meloy and illustrated by Carson Ellis, and it incorporates a number of fantasy tropes to tell an original story of a girl who discovers a hidden magical world, the eponymous Wildwood. Laika fans looked forward to seeing the film, and its gorgeous trailer only further excited moviegoers who have come to appreciate Laika’s stop-motion expertise and reputation for smart, emotionally rich storytelling. As a reminder, here’s the Wildwood trailer:

However, despite its unanimously positive reviews , Wildwood has been struggling since it hit theaters in October 2026. In its first weekend, the movie earned $12.3 million domestically, but given its $100 million production budget, Wildwood has a difficult road ahead if it hopes to turn a profit. The stakes for Laika also remain high, as the studio’s last two films have struggled at the box office. 2019’s Missing Link was released directly before Wildwood and proved to be Laika's biggest disappointment to date. That’s not to say that Wildwood can’t be a step in the right direction. It has already outperformed Missing Link , and there’s even recent precedent to believe the movie could follow in the footsteps of another 2026 movie directed by Travis Knight.

Knight currently serves as CEO of Laika, but in addition to his stop-motion work (including directing Kubo and the Two Strings ), he’s been quietly expanding to live-action filmmaking. His live-action debut came with 2018’s Bumblebee , the Transformers prequel/spinoff that easily became the most critically acclaimed film in the franchise. Earlier in 2026, he brought another beloved toy line to life with his reboot of Masters of the Universe , with Nicholas Galitzine stepping in as He-Man and Jared Leto as Skeletor. It was the first film adaptation of these characters since Dolph Lundgren and Frank Langella, respectively, played them in the infamous 1987 bomb.

Although Knight’s Masters of the Universe underperformed — bringing in only $114 million against a reported production budget as high as $200 million — it has done surprisingly well on streaming . An Amazon MGM Studios production, the movie’s performance stunned Hollywood when it arrived on Amazon Prime Video. After its theatrical run, many considered Masters of the Universe a failed attempt at launching a franchise, but now, a sequel of some kind seems much more likely. It remains to be seen if Wildwood can similarly find its audience once it hits streaming, but as of now, the movie remains a critical darling and leading Oscar contender for Best Animated Feature. With any luck, Laika’s riskiest project yet can get the attention it so richly deserves sooner rather than later.

articles.title: DC's Trinity Wouldn't Be Complete Without Wonder Woman, and These 5 Writers Helped Make It Happen
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Wonder Woman has been around for 85 years and has become one of the most important superheroes in DC Comics history. Despite her iconic status, Wonder Woman can sometimes feel like an afterthought in terms of exposure and popularity compared to her fellow Trinity members Superman and Batman. However, over the years, many writers have […]
articles.content:
Without groundbreaking storylines , massive status quo shifts, and significant character debuts, Wonder Woman wouldn’t be the most popular female superhero of all time.

Brian Azzarello might be one of the most controversial writers in Wonder Woman's history, but his impact on the character’s mythology is immeasurable. When DC Comics rebooted its universe with the New 52 initiative, Azzarello was brought on to craft a grittier and more violent reimagining of Wonder Woman. Azzarello placed far greater emphasis on the sword-wielding, warrior aspects of Wonder Woman’s character. He also made significant changes to Wonder Woman’s origin, making her the illegitimate child of Zeus and Hippolyta. The Amazons were also reimagined to be far more brutal, such as including their tradition of abducting men. Many of Azzarello’s storylines focused on the familial drama of the Greek Gods and offered incredible action set pieces. Whether the changes to Wonder Woman’s lore were good or not, they influenced all future stories and adaptations of the Princess of Themyscira. Azzarello’s portrayal helped put Wonder Woman back in the spotlight and was one of the best runs of the New 52 era.

When Wonder Woman’s popularity suffered greatly because of controversial and nonsensical stories like “Amazons Attack” in which the Amazons assaulted Washington, D.C., Gail Simone arrived to put the Princess of Themyscira back on top. Her success led to the longest tenure of any female writer on the Wonder Woman series. Despite not making any significant shifts to her status quo, Simone still wrote some of the best modern Wonder Woman stories, including “The Circle,” “Ends of the Earth,” and “Rise of the Olympian.” She delved deeper into the backstories of both Wonder Woman and the Amazons. Additionally, Simone debuted terrifying new additions to Wonder Woman’s rogues’ gallery. Genocide was a brutal Doomsday-like beast, while the Circle was a nefarious Amazonian secret society that believed that Wonder Woman would doom their people. Like the best Wonder Woman writers, Simone focused on the Princess of Themyscira as a kind, loving hero who spreads an important message of peace.

Few writers have done a better job of portraying Wonder Woman’s duality as both a peacemaker and a warrior than Greg Ruka. With heavy emphasis on Wonder Woman’s role as an ambassador for the Amazons, many of Ruka’s stories had shades of political thrillers as the Princess of Themyscira tried to resolve international tensions peacefully. Ruka also had Wonder Woman do more to try to inspire others to be their best selves. At the same time, Ruka crafted an engaging story in which Wonder Woman is pushed to the limits of her morality as she battles villains like Medusa and is even forced to fight friends like Superman and Batman. This culminates with Wonder Woman killing the telepath Maxwell Lord to save Superman and countless others. Other major shakeups by Rucka included introducing the kind-hearted minotaur Ferdinand, revealing that Wonder Woman and Cheetah were former friends, and confirming that Wonder Woman is bisexual. Altogether, Rucka delivered one of the most nuanced and inspiring runs in the Wonder Woman series.

When the Crisis on Infinite Earths rebooted the DC Universe, Wonder Woman needed a significant modernization. That reimagining came from George Perez, whom many credit as the greatest Wonder Woman writer of all time . His breakout story, “Gods and Mortals,” rebooted Wonder Woman’s origin and placed far greater emphasis on the classic Greek gods and myths that inspired her character. Perez also explored the long and complex history of the Amazons in ways that no writer had done before. He made significant status quo shifts to Wonder Woman’s character, such as giving her the ability to fly and removing her secret identity as Diana Prince. Perez also introduced some of Wonder Woman’s most iconic villains, like the Barbara Ann Minerva Cheetah, Circe, and Silver Swan. George Perez’s masterful reinvention saved Wonder Woman from cultural irrelevancy by combining classic myth with modern storytelling. In many ways, Wonder Woman wouldn’t be a member of the DC Trinity without Perez modernizing and popularizing her for a new generation.

In 1942, the idea of a female superhero taking center stage at a major comic company was practically unheard of. However, that changed when Willian Moulton Marston debuted Wonder Woman in Sensation Comics #1. Heavily inspired by his wife, Elizabeth, and their partner, Olive, Marston set out to create a superhero who was a feminist icon and an inspiration to women everywhere. Naturally, Marston laid the foundations for Wonder Woman’s origin and personality. He portrayed her as a brave, kind-hearted warrior who traveled from Paradise Island to spread a message of peace and equality to Man’s World. Marston created Wonder Woman’s most iconic tools, including the Lasso of Truth, Bracelets of Submission, and her Invisible Jet. Marston also developed Wonder Woman’s supporting cast, including Steve Trevor, Hippolyta, and Etta Candy, along with notorious villains like Ares, Priscilla Rich Cheetah, Doctor Psycho, Giganta, and Doctor Poison . Of course, Marston’s greatest contribution was making Wonder Woman one of the faces of the suffragette movement and a primary symbol of feminism in American history.

articles.title: Netflix Is About to Lose One of DC’s Best Shows and It’s Bad News For Arrowverse Fans
articles.summary: It’s been a weird week to be a DC fan. The news that James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios and that Skydance has brought in Jeremy Latcham to lead instead was a shock, but that was soon followed by rumors, reports, and speculation about what will happen to the DCU projects […]
articles.content:
The CW’s Supergirl is set to leave Netflix on December 15th, giving fans just one more month to stream the Arrowverse series. The series had already left the platform for various international markets in 2025, but this removal means it U.S. audiences will now have to look elsewhere for the series — and it’s not currently clear exactly where Kara Danvers will land next. With the series departing Netflix, the last date to stream all six seasons will be December 14th.

The idea of a series departing streaming is itself not terribly surprising. Television series leave and come back across different streaming platforms all the time and we’ve already seen the departure of some Arrowverse series from Netflix specifically — both Arrow and Black Lightning have left the platform within the past year. However, Supergirl’s departure gets us closer to all of the Arrowverse series leaving Netflix. Once Supergirl leaves, only DC’s Legends of Tomorrow and The Flash will remain. We also already know when those two shows will depart, with Legends leaving on September 2, 2027, and The Flash following on November 28, 2028.

So, why is Supergirl leaving and why have shows like Arrow and Black Lightning also left Netflix? The answer to that comes down to licensing. The existing licensing deal between The CW and Netflix is ending, which means that the shows depart as their individual deals expire. Because each series’ deal is unique, that explains the staggered expirations. On the one hand it’s good that not all of the shows are leaving at once, but it certainly is disappointing for fans who had in previous years enjoyed having the majority of the Arrowverse in one convenient place to stream. There is also a bit of silver lining when it comes to the upcoming Supergirl departure. While we don’t yet know exactly where the series will land, when Arrow left Netflix it ended up streaming for free on Pluto TV. All eight seasons of that series are currently available on that platform. It might not be a huge stretch to guess that Supergirl could end up joining it at some time in the future.

If you haven’t previously watched all six seasons of Supergirl , it’s something you should definitely do while you have the chance as it is perhaps the most underrated of the whole Arrowverse. The series initially started on CBS before jumping to The CW (which is why Supergirl took place on Earth-38 instead of the main Arrowverse Earth) and that start definitely impacted the series’ overall tone. Supergirl was a much brighter and lighter series than the rest of the Arrowverse and it very much leaned into the “hope” element of things that characters like Supergirl have built in because of the House of El symbol they wear. Even with this tonal difference, however, Supergirl is also the Arrowverse series that leaned most into its comic book elements with some truly wild stories, but also its socially conscious, politically resonant stories. Season 4 in particular introduced the villain Agent Liberty and human-alien tensions not unlike issues seen in the real world over immigration.

Supergirl also expanded the overall Arrowverse mythos in a big way when it brought Superman (played by Tyler Hoechlin) into things and, ultimately saw that hero get his own spinoff after Crisis on Infinite Earths . The biggest thing that elevates Supergirl , however, is Melissa Benoist. Her performance as Kara Danvers/Supergirl has a lot of emotional grounding and even thought the series leans into a hopeful, more positive take on the character than what we more recently saw from Milly Alcock in the DCU's Supergirl (which, mind you, was also a very well-done portrayal; there’s room for two kinds of Supergirl) Benoist also layered in some of the trauma and seriousness that goes with a character whose entire world ended and who lost her entire family. The supporting cast and characters are great, too. It’s a must-watch for any DC fan — just make sure you do so before December 15th.

Will you be binge watching Supergirl before it leaves Netflix? I’m personally revisiting Season 4 but let us know what season you liked the most in the comments.

articles.content:
After a weekend of flight delays, Hollywood's 2027 awards season is finally ready for take-off. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is kicking off the Oscars race in Los Angeles with its 17th Governors Awards , a major campaign stop for contenders looking to mingle with Academy governors representing its 19 branches. Creatives behind sweeping spectacles like "The Odyssey" and "La Bola Negra" to intimate dramas like "Wild Horse Nine" and "The Debut" will walk the red carpet before the star-studded ceremony, where some of Hollywood's most accomplished veterans will receive long-overdue accolades from their peers. Glenn Close , who has earned eight competitive acting nominations over her career (four for Best Actress, another four for Best Supporting Actress), will finally receive an Oscar recognizing her decades of awards-caliber performances. Ridley Scott , a three-time Best Director nominee for "Thelma & Louise," "Gladiator" and "Black Hawk Down," will not attend in person but will accept his honorary Oscar through a prerecorded video. Also receiving an honorary Oscar is animator Floyd Norman, best known for his work on Disney classics including "The Jungle Book" and "Sleeping Beauty," while Killer Films producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler will receive the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award. articles.title: See Candace Cameron Bure’s Sweet Reaction To BTS Full House Footage Of Her And Bob Saget
articles.summary: Oh my lanta, I'm gonna cry!
articles.content:
While it’s been over three decades since the final Full House episode aired, DJ Tanner actress Candace Cameron Bure still feels her TV “family” is important to her . So, you can only imagine how emotional the TV actress’s tribute was for her TV dad, Bob Saget, on the fourth anniversary of his death this year. If you want to get more in your feels, Bure shared her sweet reaction to BTS footage showing her and Saget on set. Fans, prepare to bring out the tissues.

I just want to cry seeing the late stand-up comic introduce the former child star as his “TV daughter” as their arms are wrapped around each other. The emotions were already present when the Great American Media actress honored Saget through a series of photos . With each picture, it was clear that Saget didn't need to be Danny Tanner to show affection to his co-stars.

The Full House alums truly appeared to have a friendship that stood the test of time. In fact, you could have called their friendship unlikely , as Bure couldn’t get into Saget's raunchy stand-up material. However, she said it was easy to be her TV dad’s friend, as she told herself to separate the comedian’s material from the "kindness" and "love" he brought out. Because the talented actress had known Saget since she was 11, it was no wonder they were still so close by the time the latter passed.

articles.title: After 49 Years, It's Easy to See Why Star Wars: A New Hope Is the "Greatest Work of Fiction Ever"
articles.summary: A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away, George Lucas dreamed up an entire universe where space wizards, droids, and countless alien species exist, all anchored by a farmboy who dreamed of something bigger. And ever since its game-changing release in 1977, Star Wars — itself partly influenced by the Flash Gordon and Buck […]
articles.content:
Of course, Star Wars itself has continued as well. Lucas’ original film was soon followed by not only two sequels to round out the original trilogy but also a prequel trilogy Lucas directed himself. Since he sold Lucasfilm — and, by extension, Star Wars — to Disney, the studio has released an additional six movies, several TV series , and countless other offshoots. Given the abundance of Star Wars projects in recent years, some fans might forget just how impactful that original film was. In fact, one surprising source even recently proclaimed Lucas’ 1977 film is the “greatest work of fiction ever.” But does that grand claim actually hold true?

Of course, it’s no big revelation to point out that Star Wars left an indelible mark on cinema. Its enduring popularity says a lot about its role in shaping all the storytelling that followed. However, too few of the analyses about Star Wars ’ success and impact hinge on its own influences , the ones that Lucas brought together to create his universe. But on a recent episode of the podcast What Now? with Trevor Noah , comedian Jimmy Carr of all people laid out his reasoning for why Lucas’ original Star Wars film stands as the “greatest work of fiction ever.” See the clip below:

Although Carr presents his argument as a “hot take,” his rationale is fascinating. Rather than giving Star Wars the title of “greatest work of fiction ever” simply based on what’s come after, he positions it as the fulcrum point of storytelling as a whole. Sure, other investigations of myth, legend, and the hero’s journey predate Lucas’ version, and certainly many more have followed in its footsteps . But Star Wars captures so many fundamentals of classical storytelling and brought them to the masses in such epic fashion that it makes sense why Carr would elect the film as essentially representative of all fiction. His breakdown even alludes to nuanced touches in both Joseph Campbell and James Joyce’s work that fall neatly in line with Lucas’ famous refrain regarding echoes within the Skywalker Saga: “It’s like poetry; they rhyme.”

So if Star Wars — that is, the 1977 film now known as Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope — is the “greatest work of fiction ever,” does it still hold on to that title nearly 50 years on? Certainly, the film and the franchise it inspired still has legions of passionate fans . However, is it possible that the sheer volume of everything Star Wars released since Lucas’ original vision has diluted the impact of that first movie? Quite possibly. After all, what started as a two-hour distillation of the hero’s journey and all the tropes of myth and legend it encompasses has now expanded into countless hours of entertainment across film, TV, video games, books, and virtually every other form of media. How can one movie continually stand out among an entire multimedia franchise?

The disappointing response to Disney+ series like The Acolyte and the underwhelming box office for The Mandalorian and Grogu — the first Star Wars film since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker — indicate that the masses are suffering from a bit of Star Wars fatigue. It’s wild to think that the fan base that was once begging for fresh content, particularly during the 1983 to 1999 stretch between Lucas’ trilogies, is opting out of the latest Star Wars projects. That said, this universe has endured rough patches before and is probably just awaiting the right project to return the franchise to its former glory. Perhaps Star Wars: Starfighter will do the trick. In any case, fans shouldn’t forget where it all began and how beautifully the original film encapsulates so much of what they love about these kinds of stories.

So is the original Star Wars the “greatest work of fiction ever”? Why or why not? Sound off below!

articles.title: DC's Next Great Superhero Could Come From Atlantis (But It's Not Aquaman)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC Comics is hitting like a magnetic accelerator cannon lately, throwing explosively entertaining stories at readers at what feels like a considerable percentage of the speed of light. It feels like every time you turn around, they have put out another brilliant comic, helping DC finally take the top sales spot from Marvel. One of […]
articles.content:
An interesting example of this is Aquaman . The King of Atlantis returned to solo book splendor in 2025, with Jeremy Adams, the writer who helped bring back Wally West and Hal Jordan in preceding years, and John Timms bringing him back for another go at stardom. The two of them redefined the character, giving him control of the Blue, the universal force related to water and the sea. It shows just how good DC has gotten at taking characters that hadn't had a lot of love lately and making them into fan-favorites. As someone who has owned several volumes of The DC Encyclopedia , the DC Multiverse's history is full of amazing characters who could make a comeback and one who's time has finally come again is Arion.

One of the things that modern comic fans who don't really know much about the history of comics is that superheroes weren't always the focus of mainstream comics in the Silver and Bronze Ages. Back then, we still had cowboy stories, fantasy stories, horror stories, and all kinds of other settings that used the same kinds of stories as superheroes – the battle of good and evil. DC was especially fruitful with its characters; over the years we got everything from cavemen to pirate heroes to Vikings that fought alongside Native Americans.

Warlord was a book that starred Travis Morgan, a military veteran who fell into the world of Skartaris (basically, late '70s/early '80s Western isekai). It was more of a fantasy-flavored book, swords and sorcery instead of tights and evil scientists, and it was in this book that Arion first appeared. Issue #55 advertised an extra “thrilling adventure in ancient Atlantis”, with Paul Kupperberg and Jan Duursema taking readers back to 45,000 BC, when Atlantis was still above the waves, an amazing magical civilization with Ahri'ahn acting as the court mage and protector of the kingdom, foiling a plot to steal the throne.

Arion back-up stories in Warlord proved to be a hit and led into Arion, Lord of Atlantis , the series running 35 issues. His stories became a new mythology for DC's Atlantis, showing it back when it was the center of magic on Earth. He was brash and powerful, basically the Atlantean version of Merlin, the powerful, ancient magic user who protected the throne and saved the day. He even showed up in Crisis on Infinite Earths (which is where I first encountered him), but the character would fade away in the days after Crisis . DC was going in a more Marvel-inspired direction and Arion, Warlord, and Amethyst all went the way of the dodo.

However, Arion was positioned as one of the greatest magic users in DC history and an important part of Atlantean lore. He would return in Peter David's The Atlantis Chronicles and would show up in flashback stories in David's Aquaman and numerous other books. There was even a time when Power Girl was thought to be related to him somehow. He was one of those characters that if you were a hardcore DC fan, you probably knew who he was but you rarely actually read any stories with him in it. When he showed up in Kurt Busiek and Carlos Pacheco's fantastic “Camelot Falls”, I remember getting that thrill of finally getting to read an all-new story with Arion in it.

In “Camelot Falls”, Arion came back in time to show Superman that his presence would cause a battle that would devastate the Earth, and his own death would come at the cost of humanity's last hope. He wanted Supes to big picture look at his life and decide whether possible ruin was worth him battling evil. It played perfectly into the imperious type of leader that Arion was, a pragmatic magic user used to making the hard choices for his kingdom and holding everyone to the same standards he set for himself. Since then, there have been few major Arion stories.

If you look across DC's line right now, you're seeing a lot of old school characters and teams returning – Deadman, Fury of Firestorm, Doom Patrol, Legion of Superheroes, Zatanna, Batwoman, Lobo . They're all somewhat popular characters that were thought to be past their best days with their new series showing that there was more gas left in their tank. Arion doesn't have their name recognition – he is an ancillary character in a less-popular portion of the DC Multiverse that hasn't had a solo book since the '90s – however, DC is ready to take chances.

We're getting books starring Jonah Hex and the Demon, and they're about on the same level as Arion. Right now, DC is rebuilding its magic comics ; Deadman is about the souls of the dead in horror-tinged mystery stories, Zatanna is big-time magical superhero action, and The Demon is shaping up to be monster-fighting madness. The publisher is showing the different facets of their magical characters and Arion would fit perfectly with them. He's the Merlin, the stormcrow who shows up when things are looking bad and shows you that they're going to get worse if you don't listen to him. He's the missing ingredient and it's time for him to shine again.

Right now, DC is doing everything right. It's impossible to look at their line and find any major problems with their books. It's all good right now and it's time to start taking chances. Arion is exactly the kind of character that DC could make a big deal right now. He's an all-powerful magic user from the days of yore, a character who you can do awesome swords and sorcery stories with as well as bring him to the present to tell cool stories with him a la “Camelot Falls”.

With Zatanna, The Demon, and Deadman each taking their own corners of magical DC, an Arion book could go in another direction. Arion is the guy who is too powerful for his own good, constantly trying to push events in the direction he wants them to go. Sometimes, he makes things better and sometimes he makes things worse and has to fix his screw-ups. He's a character who can explore the length and breadth of the DC Multiverse, making him the perfect next step in DC's domination.

Do you remember Arion? Would you like to see him show up in DC Comics again? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: I Just Learned There’s A Project Hail Mary Video Game, And Rocky’s Role Sounds ‘Amaze’
articles.summary: Fans are really going to want to try this out.
articles.content:
Plenty of films left impressions on the 2026 movie schedule , but few managed to really hit the zeitgeist like Project Hail Mary did. Phil Lord and Chris Miller ’s science-fiction epic – based on Andy Weir’s 2021 book of the same name – managed to capture audiences’ imaginations (and make some solid money at the box office in the process). Anyone who needs further proof of the film’s popularity should know that a mixed-reality game is in the works and, to quote Rocky, the description of his role sounds “amaze.”

Players can interact with objects, steer the titular ship (Hail Mary), repair it and even complete tasks like opening cupboards. One also only needs a headset to further immerse themselves in the game’s story, which was also talked out with Weir. Of course, all the while, fans can also interact with Rocky (who is not a pet) throughout their travels, and he’ll be actively watching your moves and providing feedback. Gameplay lead Sandy Lockie told SFX this about bringing Rocky and Grace’s relationship to the game:

It just wouldn’t have made sense to craft a game like this without including Rocky in some form or fashion. Since the film’s release he’s become something of a sensation, and he went viral after Amazon posted a video of the character watching himself . Even Neil DeGrasse Tyson praised the character’s design and noted that Weir and the filmmakers avoid the Hollywood trope of making him a humanoid. Judging by Lockie’s comments, even the Maze Theory team was taken with Rocky while they were testing the game:

All in all, this game should provide fans with a bit of a taste of being in Ryland’s shoes and present the opportunity to catch up with Rocky in some sense. Project Hail Mary ’s ending may have closed the book on Grace and Rocky’s bromance for now, but I still like the idea of people being able to create their own moments reminiscent of the film’s best scenes . So, on that note, why not jump into this sweet-sounding extension of the PHM story?

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers' Skeletal Transformation on 'SNL' Wasn't Just a Startling Special Effect — It Emotionally Elevated One of the Best Pop Songs Ever Written About Death
articles.summary: On her first appearance as a solo artist on "Saturday Night Live" since 2021. Phoebe Bridgers didn't break any guitars this time. But maybe some hearts. Or perhaps the impact was felt more as a chill down the spine. However it was received, Bridgers' performance of "Still Standing" turned out to be a spooky stunner, […]
articles.content:
On her first appearance as a solo artist since 2021 on “ Saturday Night Live ,” Phoebe Bridgers didn't break any guitars this time. But maybe some hearts.

Or perhaps the impact was felt more as a chill down the spine. However it was received, Bridgers' performance of “Still Standing” turned out to be a spooky stunner, pairing her already personal and emotional lyrics with the coup de grace no one saw coming: her face's sudden transformation into a skull.

If this were any halfway-standard “SNL” musical number, the visually shocking special might have seemed like a belated Halloween stunt. But “Still Standing” is an extraordinary piece of work, focused, as any serious fan well knows, on her father's death. So at a key moment near the end of the solo acosutic performance, the abrupt transition gave an extra jolt of life, so to speak, to one of the best modern pop songs ever written about death and how we process it.

On the most mundane (but still fascinating level), there's the question of how they pulled it off. It was a practical effect, and not a digital one. Bridgers was wearing UV-sensitive skull makeup under her other makeup for her entire time on “SNL,” including her preceding number. The changeover almost felt like a jump cut, but it was black lights making the hidden skull come alive.

It was spooky, but spooky with a point: Without trying to put too definite a meaning on it, it was as if Bridgers was having to go over to the other side, herself, to figure out how to grapple with a semi-estranged family member's passing and legacy, since trying to get that right on this side of the veil is a pretty effed-up mess.

Besides “Still Standing” having been a widely picked-over standout track on her recent “Lost Horizon” album, it's been at the forefront of many fans' minds because of the central place it has on the “Lost” tour that just swung through U.S. arenas. On a nightly basis, the most intimate moment has come when Bridgers would sit on the B-stage and confide a few thoughts about her dad's death — unshared to social media, since phones were locked up — before singing this most confessional of confessional numbers. If they gave Grammys for Most Beautifully Shocking Number That Is Barely Whispered, “Still Standing” would be the shoo-in.

The song deals casually and yet joltingly with a past history of family abuse, physical and psychological, as well as just indifference, and how a child perceives it all. Mixed emotions come at nearly every turn in the lyric: “You tried to make me afraid / We were both shining.” In the final stanza, she emphasizes the finality of someone disappearing off the earth forever, as she does elsewhere on the album, refusing to sentimentalize any aspect of it: “Sometimes I want you back / But not today… / I can't imagine you dead / But you are every day / Thank you for everything.” The details are specific, but probably more people than not will be able to relate to the emotion at some point in their lives, of how much to grieve someone who caused a lot of grief in his lifetime. That's all heavy stuff… and heavier when the final plaintive notes have a skeleton singing close up to you on your TV screen.

But it was also only natural that, if she was going to sing the saddest song from her album, she would counter it with the happiest: “Bobby.” That contrast is endemic to the entire album, which is fueled just as much the ebullience of a growing relationship (with Bo Burnham unmistakably understood to be the Bobby in question) as by the darkness that comes with losing one of the crucial figures in your life. Albums don't get much more yin-yang than “Lost Weekend,” and with two slots to fill on “SNL” — and a lively band in tow to help fill the one for “Bobby” — Bridgers got to reestablish her breadth in the briefest and best way possible. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The “SNL” version of “Bobby” was pretty close in spirit to the recorded version, but with one crucial difference: more yelling. For a moment or two, she got so close to a scream, it seemed like she might break into “I Know the End,” the song where she and the audience traditionally really let it all out. But this was happy howling. “This could be the end of wanting,” she sang in the refrain, and then just “This could be the end,” over and over, this time as a promise instead of a threat. In contrast to the other song choice, it was great to so vividly see and hear a Bridgers who's in the delightful throes of just knowing the beginning.

articles.title: 5 '80s Fantasy Movies That Are Required Viewing, Including the Decade's Most Traumatizing Movie
articles.summary: The versatility and greatness of the fantasy genre is something pretty underrated in the world of movies. Some of the greatest films ever released are from the genre, like The Lord of the Rings, The Wizard of Oz, Beauty and the Beast, and Spirited Away, yet people sometimes overlook these movies and focus more on […]
articles.content:
One thing that a lot of the best fantasy movies from the '80s share is that they likely traumatized thousands of children everywhere. There's just something about the fantasy genre that brings with it a fair bit of trauma and we mean that in a good way. Many fantasy films tend to feature elements that will stick with kids for a long time, even into adulthood, because they're haunting, a little creepy, and often include a memorable moment like a death or something along those lines. One of these '80s classics likely haunted more kids than any other and remains required viewing.

When it comes to weird fantasy stories, not many names are more associated with that concept than Jim Henson. His wacky concepts and sometimes unsettling looking puppets became a staple of the genre over the years. One of the best showcases of this is 1986's Labyrinth , which was directed by Henson and follows a teen girl as she enters the titular labyrinth to rescue her younger brother from the Goblin King.

The premise feels familiar, though it was relatively fresh when Labyrinth came out. The things that make this film truly great are Henson's surreal world-building and practical puppetry. They are the kind of aspects that age remarkably well and are still great to see today. Labyrinth also features an incredibly charismatic performance from the iconic David Bowie as Jareth. Reviews were mixed upon release, but the movie has gained more acclaim as time goes on, becoming a cult classic and something that everyone needs to see at least once.

It's important not to look past animation when it comes to the best fantasy films. Animation shouldn't be overlooked for any genre, but especially fantasy. They just work so perfectly together, which is evidenced by The Secret of NIMH , as the movie manages to craft a beautiful and unique world through its animation style. Based on the novel Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH, the story centers on a widowed mouse who moves her family to escape a farmer's plow.

We watch that harrowing journey as she faces challenge after challenge in this mythical world of animals, all while trying to keep her kids safe. The 1982 movie comes from animation legend Don Bluth and tells one of those timeless stories that anyone from any era can relate to and enjoy. Critics appreciated this, and though the box office numbers were disappointing, The Secret of NIMH found new life on home video.

As noted, among these required fantasy film viewings is one movie that could be considered the most traumatizing of the '80s. That is The Neverending Story , which is based on the first half of a 1979 novel of the same name. It's a wonderful adventure that captured the imagination of children everywhere, as they saw themselves in Bastian Balthazar Bux, a boy who discovers a magical book that tells the story of a young warrior who must stop a dark force from taking over the world of Fantasia.

Kids also may have seen themselves in Atreyu, the warrior at the heart of the story. Either way, they were locked into this 1984 classic. The film features the tragic death of Atreyu's trusty and beloved horse, Artax, in the Swamps of Sadness, which is a scene that scarred viewers everywhere. The haunting moment is probably the film's most memorable, but the overall project is a legitimate classic.

Jim Henson is so crucial to the legacy of the fantasy genre that he has two '80s flicks that are required viewing. A couple of years before Labyrinth , he and fellow iconic puppeteer Frank Oz came together for The Dark Crystal in 1982. This one featured even more puppets than Labyrinth and is set on a fictional planet. The story follows two Gelflings who embark on a quest to restore balance to their homeworld and overthrow an evil ruler.

Again, that's a story that has been told time and time again, yet the world of The Dark Crystal is just incredible to experience. To craft an entire world completely populated by puppets and featuring no humans is astonishing. The fact that the story works so well on top of those elements is what makes The Dark Crystal a true classic . It's another case of reception being stronger as time goes on and this even spawned an Emmy-winning modern prequel series.

The Princess Bride is basically everything you could want in a fantasy story. It starts innocently enough as a grandfather reads an epic novel to his grandson before bed. The story from the book is the events of The Princess Bride , which sees a swashbuckling farmhand team up with companions he meets along the way to rescue a princess from an evil prince. While that sounds like a story we've all seen a ton of times, it's the best iteration of that tale.

The 1987 film from Rob Reiner features exciting swordfights, a touching romance, fantastical characters, and a sharp script. The end result is a glorious fantasy tale filled with action, comedy, romance, and more. The Princess Bride holds an outstanding 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and is widely considered one of the best fantasy films ever made and one of the best movies from the '80s, regardless of genre. It has withstood the test of time and is a must-see for any fan of cinema.

Which fantasy movie from the '80s is your favorite? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Free Nintendo Switch Online Game Boy Game Celebrates 35th Anniversary
articles.summary: 1991 was 35 years ago. The dominant video game console on the market was the SNES. Its rival was the Sega Genesis. There was also the Neo Geo AES and the TurboGrafx-16. Plus, some NES consoles were still definitely floating around. There were handhelds too, including the Sega Game Gear and the Atari Lynx. Like […]
articles.content:
Those who had a Game Boy in 1991 were probably playing the likes of Metroid II: Return of Samus, Mega Man: Dr Wily's Revenge, Final Fantasy Adventure, Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge, Operation C , and a few others, including Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters . Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters, for those who do not recognize the name, is an action platformer from Tose and Nintendo, and the sequel to 1986's Kid Icarus , created by Satoru Okada, the creator of the Game Boy, who was also instrumental in the creation of Metroid and was the creator of Super Mario Land . The 79-year-old industry pioneer has been retired from Nintendo and the industry since 2012.

Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters was one of the standout games of 1991, and easily one of the great Game Boy games as well. 35 years later, it's celebrating its anniversary this month, and while it's not available natively on Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2, it is available via Nintendo Switch Online . And unlike some Nintendo Switch Online games, it does not require the Expansion Pack to access.

A Classic From a Different Era of Gaming It doesn't appear Nintendo is going to do anything for the anniversary, and it's not very invested in the Kid Icarus series in general. To date, we've gotten three games in it that were released in 1986, 1991, and 2012. To this end, it's been dormant for 14 years. Fans with a Nintendo Switch Online subscription can celebrate the anniversary with a free download of not just it, but the first game as well.

Does Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters hold up in 2026? Well, if you have no experience with the original Game Boy, probably not. The Game Boy was a very impressive machine for its time, but it's also a very rudimentary machine. Most of its catalog, as a result, has not aged terribly well. Those without Game Boy nostalgia probably are not going to enjoy visiting Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters for the first time in 2026. Those who do, though, it's a potent dose of nostalgia, and because the game is only 2 to 4 hours long, it can easily be beaten in a single weekend, if not a single day, making it accessible for many.

Looking ahead for Nintendo Switch Online, there probably aren't many Game Boy games still coming, but it does look like 3DS may be added as a platform soon, and bring with it one of the great Legend of Zelda games . That said, three Game Boy games were recently added , but Nintendo is starting to scrape the bottom of the barrel of the games it will be reasonably able to obtain for the subscription service.

articles.title: Disney Boss Wants an Avengers-Inspired Team-Up for Iconic Animation Characters
articles.summary: It seems that an Avengers Assemble-style team-up has been on everyone's minds recently, spanning genres and mediums (Crescent City 3, anyone?), with everyone wanting to bring together the best of the best to take on a new challenge or villain. And even Disney animation isn't immune to the trendy desire, with Disney's Chief Creative Officer […]
articles.content:
Collider’s Steve Weintraub got ahold of Bush at this year's SCAD Savannah Film Festival, asking the award winner in charge of projects like Encanto and Zootopia , “What are the chances of doing an Avengers-style team-up with a number of Disney animated characters that somehow come together in one movie and work together to do something?” Bush responded, “I like the idea of that. I will not give you credit for it if we ever do it, but I like that idea.” The idea, while not entirely original, hearkens back in some ways to Wreck-It Ralph , which people loved—especially the aspect that had characters from across the stories' universe coming together.

With the likes of Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Doomsday seeming to have taken all the spotlight (though some has still been left for the live-action adaptation of Tangled ), fans of the animated stories have been left a little adrift. But Bush says that there's tons to look forward to on the horizon . “There is something we've actually been working on. It is a special set in the world of The Princess and the Frog . We are really moving on that right now. So, that's actually in active production. That will be out to people soon. New songs. Original cast. It is pretty spectacular,” he said about one of the more exciting projects that's coming to Disney+ soon.

There's also more Wreck-It Ralph planned, with an attraction making its way to Tokyo. And we can't forget the upcoming Zootopia 3 , which is going to get Judy and Nick out of the city and on new adventures. When asked about his involvement in that particular project, Bush said, “This is something that is going to take a lot of time to get right. I think with any movie set in the world of Zootopia , Judy and Nick are going to be at the very center of that. I think people know at this point that we are going to introduce birds into the world of Zootopia , and I think this may be the first time that we travel outside the bounds of Zootopia City itself.”

There's also Frozen 3 right around the corner; the threequel is scheduled to be released next year. And obviously, Hexed is the next big thing on the docket, hitting theaters on November 25th.

If you could team up any iconic Disney animated characters for the ultimate Doomsday-esque showdown, which would you pick? Let us know your choices in the comments.

articles.title: Henry Cavill's Forgotten R-Rated Historical Action Adventure Is Finding Streaming Success After 15 Years
articles.summary: Courtesy of Relativity Media For many people Henry Cavill is still associated with his appearance as Superman in Zack Snyder's DC movies to the point that much of what he has done outside the role has either gone unnoticed or been forgotten. The later can be said of his first major leading role in a violent Greek myth action […]
articles.content:
Immortals combines the mythological stories of Theseus and the Minotaur with the Titanomachy to create its own story. The film takes place in a time when the power-hungry King Hyperion (Rourke) is waging a war across Greece in order to acquire the Epirus Bow, a legendary weapon that can release the Titans from their mountain prison and destroy the gods of Mount Olympus. Unable to directly stop Hyperion, Zeus (Evans) tutors mortal Theseus (Cavill) to rally his own army to take down Hyperion and his forces. While the story may have been told in several ways over the years, the question is does Cavill's version bring anything new to the table or was it just another retread of the same old story? Most people couldn't make up their minds.

Immortals is a movie that was not able to avoid comparisons to Zack Snyder's 300 with everything from its brutal slow motion fight scenes to costumes and set designs. While this was something that famously bothered director Tarsem Singh – who pointed out in many interviews that his movie actually filmed on real sets and not with the green screen of Snyder's movie – it did not stop the film making three times its $75 million budget back at the box office with a worldwide haul of over $226 million. However, when it came to its reviews both critics and audiences were completely split down the middle.

For many critics, the film looked good but had nothing else worth praising. This is something that Roger Ebert alluded to in his 2-star rating, in which he noted that Immortals was “without doubt the best-looking awful movie you will ever see.” Yet, for all its faults, the film has some big set piece moments that have set it up as a cult movie for those who have discovered it in the last decade and a half. While that does not detract from the flaws in its scripting and pacing as it offers enough for those looking for a timewaster movie on streaming to give it watch.

Cavill obviously went onto bigger things just a few years later when he donned the cape of Superman in Man of Steel . While he has not returned to play the lead in anything quite as epic or brutal as Immortals , he is about to step into several new potential franchises in the coming years with his appearances in the Highlander reboot, a Warhammer 40K TV series , and his Voltron movie. While you are waiting for all that, then you might as well join the many to have already checked out Immortals on Prime Video.

Have you seen Immortals ? How does it fare against other sword and sandal movies for you? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X Update Released With New Feature for OG Xbox Fans
articles.summary: As part of ongoing celebrations for the 25th anniversary of Xbox, Microsoft has released a new Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S update with a new feature for nostalgic fans of the original Xbox, often referred to as the OG Xbox. While the new special 25th anniversary Xbox Series X is not available to […]
articles.content:
More precisely, Microsoft has gone ahead and released the original Xbox boot-up animation for all Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, and Xbox One players. The boot-up animation is free, and doesn't require any download. By the end of the day, everyone will simply find it in their settings going forward. According to Microsoft, this is just a “thank you” for 25 years of Xbox. Below, you can check out the new animation for yourself.

In addition to the original Xbox boot-up animation, there are now also two additional Xbox 360 boot-up animations as well. So, three new animations in total, all nostalgic for those who have been with Xbox through their first two console generations and their two best console generations as well.

We’re bringing back the original XBOX boot-up animation for all XBOX Series X|S and XBOX One players, along with two additional XBOX 360 boot-up animations! This update will be rolling out throughout the day and thank you for being part of 25 years of XBOX. pic.twitter.com/V9SKMZTtPR

As you would expect, Xbox fans are excited for this update. You can see this in the engagement on the post above, as Xbox posts on X rarely get that many likes that quickly. The comments are all positive as well. And this makes sense. The original Xbox is pure nostalgia for many of the most hardcore fans, while the Xbox 360 was not just the peak of Xbox, but this era of gaming in general was arguably the peak of the industry. “Grown men about to restart their Series X 40 times tonight just to feel like it's 2002 again,” reads the top comment on the X post above. Another adds, “The 360 boot-up sound is pure 2007. Hearing it again is going to send me straight back to Halo 3 nights.”

A third comment reads, “I think it's time I buy an Xbox.” Meanwhile, a fourth comment further drives home the point: “That boot sound is the closest thing gaming has to a national anthem.”

As far as we can tell, these are permanent additions to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S consoles. Meanwhile, this follows PlayStation doing the same thing , but with PS1, PS2, PS3, and PS4 when it had its own anniversary recently.

articles.title: First HBO Harry Potter Clip Splits the Fandom But Proves The Show Does One Thing Better Than The Movies
articles.summary: HBO has released the first full clip from their upcoming Harry Potter TV series - and while there's good news, not every fan is embracing the new clip. From the outset, the promise of the new series has been a deeper dive into the Wizarding World and the Boy Who Lived - bringing back fan-favorite […]
articles.content:
The abandonment of the Fantastic Beasts “trilogy” after part two, the casting of Paapa Essiedu as Snape , J.K. Rowling's increasingly divisive foray into social issues, and the general sentiment that it's “too soon” for an “unnecessary” remake have split the Harry Potter fandom – a pattern that is further evidenced by reactions to the new clip.

The clip itself was officially released by HBO in anticipation of the new series – which launches on Christmas Day – and features an extended version of Harry, Ron, and Hermione's first night feast, following the Sorting Hat ceremony.

Check out the official clip below, titled “The Start of the Term Banquet Clip”:

While the clip sticks relatively close to what was depicted in the film, there are subtle and not-so-subtle additions , the largest and most important being exactly what HBO claims justifies retelling the story: more time to explore moments between characters and the dynamics behind them – as evidenced by the small but telling exchange between Albus Dumbledore and Minerva McGonagall, played by John Lithgow and Janet McTeer, respectively.

The interaction tells us additional details that the movie adaptation did not have space to set up, specifically calling attention to McGonagall's affection for the Potter family and acknowledgement that Harry is the spitting image of James – a detail that was a throughline in the books but less so in the films. After all, in the films James and Lily were depicted as older than they were in the novels – a change the TV series is set to undo with a younger set of actors portraying the couple .

In comparison, you can check out a clip from the original film below, which focuses on Nearly Headless Nick interrupting the ceremony, and saved budget on the food “appearing” via a cutaway crane shot – rather than tableside CGI effects.

The juxtaposition of the two clips emphasizes the heavy lifting a movie scene needs to do – introducing multiple concepts and characters in a few minutes (in this case, adding Nearly Headless Nick) where the show doesn't have to force him in – and makes extra room for extra character building between Dumbledore and McGonagall.

That all said, the new clip was not met with universal acclaim. While some fans celebrated the additional character development and were reassured by Harry and Ron's reactions to the feast erupting from their table (from YouTube : “ The little conversation between Dumbledore and Mcgonagall gives us more of an example of how this show will give more outside of Harry's point of view on things than the books or movies did “), others took the opportunity to voice displeasure at the quality of the clip itself, Rowling, or new HBO owner David Ellison:

The no candles hurts. Looks like a Walmart food ad

The series launches on HBO Max in just six weeks – and marketing for the show is just starting to get traction – but this early sneak peek seems to suggest that, while the series is likely to be a massive viewership draw, it's still struggling to unite a fractured fan base.

So Hoffman stayed on, but still had serious doubts. They went on for a few days, and Hoffman was still frustrated, unable to really find Raymond’s core.

This goes on for reel after reel, and Hoffman still isn’t feeling it. He went one:

What Levinson had found in those scenes was that Hoffman had Ray. Hoffman realized that Levinson was right. He had found the character, and the rest is history. articles.title: GTA 6's Enormous Download Size Prompts Publishers to Post In-Game Messages Asking Players Not to Delete Their Games
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games EA is taking an unusual approach to keeping players engaged with Madden NFL 27 ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, with players reporting an in-game message asking them not to delete the game. Titled "Don't Delete!", the pop-up teases an upcoming November 17 update, telling players that a crew is assembling for a "high-stakes […]
articles.content:
The connection to GTA 6 isn't explicitly stated in the pop-up, though EA has already made its awareness of Rockstar's enormous upcoming release abundantly clear. On November 10, the official Madden NFL account posted , “Don't let 210GB get between you and Your League,” directly referencing the storage space players may need for GTA 6. Rockstar has confirmed that the game's pre-load can require up to 212GB, depending on the platform. Culture Crave shared the in-game message on X , showing the rather unusual request players are now encountering in Madden NFL 27

The presentation is particularly funny because EA has seemingly embraced the comparison rather than simply letting its earlier social media post do the talking. The pop-up's language and visual presentation evoke GTA 6's criminal escapades, while the request itself is about as straightforward as marketing gets. Players are being asked to keep Madden installed, and the publisher has even given them a date to look forward to before Rockstar's game arrives.

It's also a rather unusual thing to see inside a game. Publishers routinely promote upcoming updates and seasonal content, but an explicit “Don't Delete!” message is a considerably more memorable way to do it. There is no shortage of games competing for players' time, but GTA 6's reported storage requirements add another dimension to that competition. Some players will inevitably have to make room for the new release, and Madden NFL 27 is making a playful case for why it shouldn't be among the games they remove.

Games come and go. Players finish a release, move on to something else, and occasionally circle back when new content arrives. That's an entirely normal part of the medium, particularly when another major release is about to consume everyone's attention. Yet the idea that a publisher might need to remind its audience not to delete a game is a pretty remarkable reflection of how competitive the modern live-service environment has become.

Of course, EA is clearly having some fun with the situation, and the November 17 teaser gives the message a purpose beyond simply acknowledging GTA 6's looming arrival. Still, it's hard not to appreciate the absurdity of a major publisher effectively asking players to save some space for its game when one of the industry's biggest releases is about to arrive. GTA 6 hasn't even launched yet, and it's already prompting some unexpected marketing from elsewhere in the industry.

articles.title: 3 Most Memorable Dragon Ball Villain Moments After 42 Years
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Usually the aura-farming is reserved for the good guys in Dragon Ball, but the franchise has produced some unforgettable villains too. The constant and overwhelming powering up to outmatch the Z Fighters gave the audience that sudden feeling of dread. Every time it felt like there was no way they'd overcome some of the sadistic […]
articles.content:
They ultimately find the way to victory, but it's not without losses and sometimes death amongst earth's defenders. The villains stop at nothing and regularly commit heinous acts to get their points across. That's what makes Goku and his group such a perfect foil to the enemies . The group's pure-heartedness and care for everyone else around them is where their strength lies, and these villains below took their swings at breaking them down.

Tough to top the introduction that original Broly gets in Dragon Ball Z: Broly – The Legendary Super Saiyan . The build up of him constantly yelling out, “Kakarot!,” swatting Vegeta's attacks away like a fly and ultimately transforming into the Legendary Super Saiyan, are all mind-blowing moments. Pantera's 10's breakdown kicks in perfectly, to pair up with him physically exploding into a larger Saiyan in the English dub, while screaming out before cackling like a maniac.

It's an awesome scene that makes the hair on the back of your neck stand up. Then to top it all off, Broly points at Goku and says in his gravelly voice, “You Kakarot, I choose you to the best first of my victims.” An unhinged line that he backs up quickly by dominating all the Z Fighters in the initial battle. Goku pays back the big Saiyan with a ultra-powered punch that finishes the job. Who cares that this movie is non-canon? It provided audiences with one of the best villains in the series.

From relief to sheer horror in a short time, the Z Fighters got a terrible surprise when Super Perfect Cell returned to earth. Cell threatened to blow up everyone on the planet after his loss to Gohan. Goku simply Instant Transmissions himself and Cell to King Kai's Planet to “safely-ish” detonate Cell away from earth. It looked like the move saved everyone and defeated Cell for good. Only for him to return and state that he's even stronger through all of power he absorbed from Goku and Piccolo to become the perfect organism.

His condescending tone and cocky smirk just made him an impossible-to-beat enemy. Cell made it sound like all their efforts were futile, and he brought that fear to fruition by surviving his own detonation. Cell becomes so strong that the only way to defeat him is for Gohan to hit a Kamehameha that legitimately envelops and overwhelms his enemy. The blast initially does enough damage to defeat Cell, but just to make sure, Gohan increases the power to eviscerate every last microscopic cell of Cell.

Dragon Ball Z had already started down a darker, grittier path than its predecessor, but it really turned up a few notches in the Frieza Saga. Goku sacrifices himself to help Piccolo kill Raditz , which started off the heavy plot points, but what Frieza does is burned into so many audience member's minds. The evil lord decided to punish Goku for making him battle with a low-class Saiyan. He picks up a defenseless Krillin, levitating him with a wave of his finger. He then clenches his fist together and blows up.

The effortlessness it took to for Frieza to do it, and in such a merciless manner, was blood curdling. Everything changed in a hurry, and even though he thought it would shake Goku's resolve, the Saiyan went the opposite way. The sadistic move only angered Goku more and resulted in the first ever Super Saiyan transformation. Not long after that, he defeated Frieza, bringing an end to wicked ruler. From Zendaya channeling a 2000s Halle Berry to Carmen Electra going full Catwoman , the creativity that went into each costume was truly impressive. But even though Halloween is over, actress Jessica Chastain has taken it upon herself to dress up as Jessica Rabbit. I’ve got to say, I’m surprised this is happening shortly after the spooky season, but I'm not mad at it.

In many of Chastain’s best movies, she takes on a variety of looks. Whether it’s early 20th-century garb in Crimson Peak or portraying a blonde ‘60s housewife in The Help, each film's costume really adds to her transformative performances. But I have to say that even though the Oscar winner didn't dress as Jessica Rabbit for a movie, this costume is still quite impressive. It's unclear if her Flaunt Magazine photoshoot actually happened after Halloween, but the photographer is sharing pics on his Instagram now:

Whoa, baby! I can’t believe it’s taken this long for the Zero Dark Thirty actress to dress as this sultry animated character. That shiny, silk red dress is the perfect way to show the femme fatale character’s seductive qualities. This has always been a perfect fit for her, as she’s already got the Who Framed Roger Rabbit character’s first name and her signature red locks. Now, we just need to hear Chastain sing “Why Don’t You Do Right?” and she’s a shoo-in for her own Jessica Rabbit live-action solo movie (if a studio ever chooses to greenlight one).

Of course, Jessica Chastain isn't the first person to ever channel the beloved cartoon character. This past Halloween, 90 Day Fiancé’s Kara Leona had a perfect Jessica Rabbit costume , with her dark red hair matching her red dress perfectly. Also, in 2015, Heidi Klum’s Jessica Rabbit costume looked just like the cartoon (and it was kinda scary). Chloe Bailey, dressed as Roger Rabbit’s wife for Halloween in 2024, was also very eye-popping with her sequined red dress, long purple gloves and cigarette holder.

While I think Chastain's shoot would've been well-timed for Halloween, I think it's refreshing to see her as the “Drawn That Way” icon after the fact. Her vintage, glamorous appearance is like looking at a red-headed Marilyn Monroe. It’s hard to look away.

While some may say Rabbit is too attractive for Roger , she said in Who Framed Roger Rabbit that it didn’t take much for her husband to win her over. The show-stopping cartoon simply said, “He makes me laugh.” In that way, she's not a vain character, and it's not hard to see why she's so respected.

Needless to say, Jessica Chastain was born to wear this costume, and she once again proves that she's a truly fabulous star. Here's hoping this won't be the last time she decides to channel a beloved character of any kind.

You can see why Jessica Rabbit is such a popular Halloween costume by streaming Who Framed Roger Rabbit with a Disney+ subscription . You can also watch Chastain’s new streaming release , Heartland , which is available with an active Netflix subscription .

articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero’s Most Destructive Scene Fulfilled the Director’s Childhood Dream
articles.summary: Few movie monsters can compare with the might of Godzilla. The iconic creature has starred in dozens of films since his 1954 debut and is currently headlining not one but two film franchises. In 2014, Godzilla kicked off Legendary Pictures’ Monsterverse, and Godzilla has remained one of the central figures. So far, he has clashed […]
articles.content:
In fact, 2023’s Godzilla Minus One raised the series' profile in a big way, which says a lot considering the Godzilla films hold the record for the longest-running movie franchise. The movie — directed by Takashi Yamazaki — reinvigorated the character’s appeal worldwide with a grounded, character-based reset and Academy Award-winning visual effects. In fact, Godzilla Minus One was the first movie in the series to win an Oscar in its 70-year history. So it’s remarkable that its sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero manages to up the ante with its destruction, including one sequence which was the realization of a lifelong dream for Yamazaki.

Warning: Spoilers ahead for Godzilla Minus Zero .

The story of Godzilla Minus Zero kicks off with the emergence of a terrifying new kaiju, which later becomes known as King Ghidorah . The three-headed dragon-like creature is, of course, familiar to longtime Godzilla fans, having come to blows with the King of the Monsters numerous times over the years. In fact, King Ghidorah made his debut way back in 1964’s Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster . But the character’s appearance in Godzilla Minus Zero gave Yamazaki the chance to revisit a disappointment from his own childhood. According to a recent interview, Yamazaki had hoped to see King Ghidorah destroy his hometown of Matsumoto.

Although Yamazaki was born the very same year Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster was released, it stands to reason that he would grow up with the movies as a key part of his childhood. Since Godzilla’s debut, the character has been a fan favorite for generations, gaining worldwide acclaim and sustaining popularity even during extended periods between new films. Given how much Godzilla Minus One helped reaffirm the series’ love, it makes perfect sense that Yamazaki would bring a fan’s perspective to his own Godzilla films , and by the sounds of it, he was intent on delivering the experience he most would have wanted to see.

During a key scene in Godzilla Minus Zero , Yamazaki finally revisits his lifelong fantasy of seeing King Ghidorah emerge in Matsumoto. In fact, the Japanese city is among the first to feel the fearsome kaiju’s wrath. “I had the chance to make the ⁠movie I wanted to watch back then, and I created the footage that I wanted to ​show my younger self, as if to say, ‘This is what you wanted to see, isn't it?’” Yamazaki explained to Reuters . “So, my dream has finally come true after 55 years, and I am truly happy.” So too are audiences who reveled in King Ghidorah's return to the screen. His most recent film appearance was in the 2019 Monsterverse feature Godzilla: King of the Monsters .

In the Matsumoto sequence, King Ghidorah uses his electrical beams to ravage the city, and this event leads to early efforts to destroy the creature. Of course, that attack proves ineffective, accidentally triggering King Ghidorah’s evolution into his three-headed form and gifting him the ability to lift and smash buildings for maximum destruction. Even though the film builds well beyond the initial Matsumoto attack — including an epic showdown with a resurrected Godzilla — it is cool that Yamazaki channeled his personal history with King Ghidorah into his own version of the Godzilla mythology.

Does Godzilla Minus Zero do justice to King Ghidorah’s big-screen legacy? Which other classic monsters would you like to see in a potential third entry in Yamazaki’s Godzilla series? Let us know in the comments below!

Godzilla Minus Zero is now playing in theaters.
