articles.title: Mattel's M.U.S.C.L.E. Toys Were Based on a Popular Japanese Manga, But American Kids Never Knew It
articles.summary: In 1985, Mattel brought Bandai's Kinkeshi toyline to American shelves as M.U.S.C.L.E, standing for "Millions of Unusual Small Creatures Lurking Everywhere." While the original Bandai lines came with the added context of being based the popular Kinnikuman manga and anime, the descriptor of "unusual small creatures" was the most American audiences were given, making the […]
articles.content:
Mattel's unique release strategy for M.U.S.C.L.E . made it easier for kids and challenging for completionist adults to collect. The figurines were primarily sold in completely randomized packages of four or ten, as well as larger (loosely) themed twenty-eight packs. The four-packs retailed for a lower cost than the average action figure in 1985 or '86, making it easier for a kid to amass an impressive collection of M.U.S.C.L.E . figures on a budget of spare change and their weekly allowance. Owing to their low price point, the figures are plentiful, seeming to make their way into virtually every toy collection of the era, although the first law of toy collecting dictates that as a collector edges closer to having them all, they will inevitably never come across those last five or ten missing characters. That's why auctions like this upcoming lot at Heritage advertise and emphasize having key characters like “the Claw,” a giant disembodied hand and a cult favorite of M.U.S.C.L.E . collectors, included. Given the aforementioned random release strategy, coming across the exact fan favorite character mint-on-card is exceptionally rare.

Kinnikuman was created in 1979 by Yoshinori Nakai and Takashi Shimada, and was designed by the pair as a loose parody of Ultraman . The plot followed the masked wrestler Kinnikuman (translated roughly as “Muscleman”), deposed prince of the planet Kinniku, as he competed against the wrestlers of the wicked Chojin in a quest to prove himself worthy of Kinniku's throne. Terri-Bull / Buffaloman was one of many villains Kinnikuman faced in the ring, and would become an ally to Kinnikuman after being defeated in combat. Such was also the case for Ramenman , Ashuraman , Robin Mask , and numerous other characters who appeared in the Kinkeshi (and subsequently M.U.S.C.L.E .) toylines. The Japanese name for the line, “kinkeshi,” is a portmanteau of Kinnikuman and “keshi,” a type of soft rubber, eraser-like figurine popular in Japan. Though a popular toy in Japan, keshi figures lack the same cache in the American market, meaning that when M.U.S.C.L.E . debuted, there was not another toyline like it. Its scale, designs, and open-ended world were unlike virtually anything else on the market.

It's not unusual for an American toy company to take an existing product from Japan and rebrand it for Western audiences. Most famously, this was the origin story of the Transformers , but this practice also spawned lines like Mego's Micronauts, Mattel's Shogun Warriors , and even Tonka's Go-Bots . Where M.U.S.C.L.E . varies is that it eschewed the tie-in comic book or animated series that was used by these other properties to help familiarize kids with the line and its characters. M.U.S.C.L.E , for better or for worse, was a blank slate. Mattel's marketing materials give a little background, specifying that “Muscleman and his heroic Tag Team, the Thug Busters, are ready for all challengers. The terrible Terri-Bull and his evil cohorts [sic], the Cosmic Crunchers, want to take the world to the mat.” For the most part, which characters fit into each faction was left in the hands of kids, outside of the twenty-eight designated “Thug Busters” and “Cosmic Crunchers” included in the faction-themed packs Mattel sold. Two additional twenty-eight packs, the “Mighty Maulers” and the “Cosmic Showdown” were also available.

These twenty-eight packs were less popular than the modestly-priced four-packs, and are difficult to locate on the secondary market. More common are the ten-packs, which were sold in plastic garbage cans; a fair number of kids held onto these and used them to store their M.U.S.C.L.E . collections. Additional expressions for the line enhanced the wrestling theme, with a “Hard Knockin' Wrestling Ring” playset, a wearable “Battlin' Belt” that could house a small number of M.U.S.C.L.E . figures, and the “Mega Match” game, which created turn-based gameplay for wrestling matches between the figurines. The “Hard Knockin' Wrestling Ring” had play mechanics similar to Rock ‘Em, Sock ‘Em Robots : the players clipped one figure each into a plastic stand controlled by a joystick, enabling them to “fight” until one figure was knocked loose from the plastic clip. The playset and game are relatively rare, and command triple-digits price-points mint in box.

A promotional mail-away from Mattel threw down the gauntlet for collectors: a poster featured all two hundred and thirty-three M.U.S.C.L.E . figures, emblazoned with the rhetorical question of “Can you collect them all?” As mentioned in the introduction, the randomized nature of M.U.S.C.L.E ‘s distribution meant that the answer to this was “no” for all but the most diligent, obsessive fan — and that doesn't become much easier for them, even as an adult. The lack of agreed upon names adds another degree of difficulty, as seeking out individual characters on auction sites is hampered by trying to figure out which name the seller might have the character listed under. Some American M.U.S.C.L.E . collectors have taken to using the Japanese names, while other stick with the informal nicknames adopted by the American collecting community. As an example, “the Claw” advertised by Heritage's M.U.S.C.L.E . auction listing is a collector nickname for a character known in Kinnikuman as “ Sunigator Shotai .” Some eBay listings for the figure use both names, some one or the other, some use neither.

Beyond the incredibly wide character selection, Mattel introduced another challenge to assembling a complete set of M.U.S.C.L.E . figures: different colored rubber. Later waves of M.U.S.C.L.E . came in eye-catching blues, reds, oranges, and greens. Including color variants, there are more than a thousand M.U.S.C.L.E . figures, though most collectors content themselves with trying to assemble a complete set of characters. M.U.S.C.L.E . is an easy line to collect, and a tough line to complete; each of these characteristics makes it attractive to different kinds of collectors. For some, M.U.S.C.L.E . is a fun line to informally gather a handful of from conventions, flea markets, and collectible stores. They're cheap, readily available, and full of creative, strange designs like the Moai-inspired “ Amoiman ” or the shark-headed “ Jawsman .” Patience and research might be needed to track down the line's most elusive releases, and there is nothing hardcore collectors love more than a challenge. To a lesser extent, that's also the appeal of mint-on-card auctions like the Heritage listing: it captures some of the line's best characters in a rare state of preservation, creating a unique display piece that emphasizes just what makes M.U.S.C.L.E . unique.

Do you collect M.U.S.C.L.E . figures? Leave a comment below and join the conversation now in the ComicBook Forum !

articles.summary: No one can deny the fact that Spider-Man: Brand New Day is genuinely one of the best offerings that Marvel has put out there, especially in recent years, when other films have felt a little anemic, plot-wise. It broke box office records left and right, becoming the highest-grossing film of all time (at the domestic […]
articles.content:
Or a nomination, at the very least . Speaking with Deadline, Rothman said, “The Academy is meant to recognize greatness. So, to be honest, I think it comes down to greatness. But also to receive wisdom about what greatness is. If there aren’t people thinking about it, we’re gonna do what we can just to make people think about it.” He went on to elaborate on his ideas of greatness and how that pertains to Brand New Day , adding, “Here’s what I ask people when I walk around: ‘Are you telling me that there are 10 films this year that are better than this film?’”

No doubt about it, Brand New Day is a great film, and the box office numbers speak for themselves. But does that make it inherently Oscar-worthy? Even fans of the webslinger have their doubts. “As someone who does really like this film, I still gotta say, yeah, I really think you should probably sit down, Tim,” said one. Another agreed , adding, “God, this is ridiculous. It reminds me of when they tried to pass off Wonder Woman for Best Picture.” But it seems like Rothman can't hear the haters of the 90% critics' score that the film has earned from Rotten Tomatoes, or the millions and millions of dollars it earned at the box office.

It certainly wouldn't be the first superhero movie to be nominated, or even to bring home a win. But it would need to stack up against some seriously heavy hitters, like Black Panther , The Dark Knight , and Spider-Man 2 . It's worth noting that some head-scratchers have also brought home the prestigious award, albeit in different categories, like The Joker and Suicide Squad , but to each their own, and Brand New Day could certainly hang with those two in particular. As to whether or not there are 10 better films that have come out this year, that's up to the panel of judges that hands out the awards, but even Spider-Man fans seem to think it doesn't quite hit that level of prestige, with one saying, “There are 10 films from July-August alone that are better than it. Very few superhero films are in that film-of-the-year discussion.”

articles.title: 5 Movie Sequels That Changed The Direction Of Their Franchise (2 Went In The Wrong Direction)
articles.summary: Modern cinema isn't built simply on thousands and thousands of standalone films, as franchises and sequels have proven to be incredibly successful over the years. When a movie strikes gold with a great premise and commercial or critical success, it's only natural that the creative forces behind it might want to expand upon its story. […]
articles.content:
However, just because a sequel continues the story of its predecessor doesn't mean it has to be the exact same type of movie. Some movie franchises only seem to get better with time , with each new entry helping it to evolve and change shape as it continues to grow. Others do the opposite, with quality seeming to decline as they move away from the original film's characters or ideas. There are many examples of sequels that perfectly represent the moment a franchise changed direction, and while it might not have always been for the better, it's interesting to track the specifics of their transformation.

Over the years, there have been many sci-fi sequels better than the original , and 1986's Aliens is often considered one of them. The follow-up to Ridley Scott's 1979 classic took the only human character to survive the Xenomorph's attack on the Nostromo and put her in the middle of another encounter with the dangerous creatures. Aliens might have taken its cues from the original movie, but it also made a huge change from its predecessor. Where Alien was pure claustrophobic horror, Aliens incorporated elements of sci-fi action into its plot, giving its characters a very slim chance to fight back against the Xenomorph threat. By showing just how futile fighting against the aliens appears to be, Aliens actually managed to be scary in a whole new way, taking the ideas of the original movie and transforming them into something new. Aliens is a sequel that established the franchise's action potential, nudging it in a slightly different direction than the hopeless terror of the first film and toward something much larger and more existentially terrifying.

While Vin Diesel appears in many popular movie franchises , only one is considered to be the actor's pet project. 2000's Pitch Black was a sci-fi survival horror that saw Diesel play Riddick, a dangerous convict with enhanced eyes that allow him to see in the dark. The movie followed a group of terrified survivors of a crashed spaceship attempting to survive on a world filled with hostile nocturnal creatures, with Riddick proving to be the standout character. Diesel then went on to reprise the role in sequels centering on Riddick's story, starting with 2004's The Chronicles of Riddick . The sequel was a step in a whole new direction, taking a character from Pitch Black ‘s atmospheric horror and casting him as the lead in a sprawling space opera. It was a bizarre choice, and the movie was nowhere near as successful as it might have been, going down in history as an underwhelming sci-fi flop despite having some good ideas.

The first Mad Max movie was an interesting, if somewhat unremarkable, exploration of a world that has just tipped over the brink of collapse. The sequel, The Road Warrior , took the franchise in a whole new direction, embracing its apocalyptic setting and carving for itself a whole new identity that every Mad Max movie since has followed in one way or another. While the first film undeniably laid the groundwork with its story, The Road Warrior was the film that established the true character of the franchise, embracing its eclectic visual identity and defining the sort of apocalyptic action that made Mad Max so popular. Where the first film was a revenge thriller set on the verge of society's collapse, The Road Warrior took its hero and turned him into a sort of mythological figure roaming the desert wasteland and taking the fight to its self-proclaimed warlords. In many ways, The Road Warrior marked the true beginning of the Mad Max franchise, because it was the first step in the direction that its sequels continue to head in for years to come.

The movies of the Rambo franchise are best categorized as over-the-top action stories with a single action hero at their core. Helping to popularize the one-man army trope that defined the action movies of the '80s, the Rambo franchise has become practically synonymous with a single veteran taking on forces that vastly outnumber him and emerging victorious. However, this core philosophy wasn't really present in the franchise's first — and, by most estimations, best — movie. First Blood introduced John Rambo as a misunderstood veteran living with PTSD whose appearance in a small town causes him to be unfairly hunted by corrupt law enforcement officers. The sequel, First Blood Part II , instead embraced the cheesier action tropes of the era, abandoning the original's more thought-provoking elements to deliver all-out action thrills. While the movies that followed were largely successful, none of them ever managed to recapture the sensitivity and thematic depth of the original, proving that First Blood Part II ‘s changes were indeed a step in the wrong direction.

When The Fast and the Furious was first released in 2001, many felt the film was simply Point Break but with tricked-out cars instead of surfboards. A few sequels later, Fast Five completely switched the franchise up. Where the Fast & Furious movies were originally all about people who loved racing fast cars alongside their criminal lifestyles, Fast Five took the latter part to new heights. The result made for one of the best heist movies in recent years, and the franchise embraced this new identity. From there, everything continued to get bigger and more extreme, from the heists themselves to the stunts involved in pulling them off. The Fast and Furious movies are often cited as an example of a franchise that evolved considerably across its many movies, and Fast Five was the sequel that truly started the shift. While some lament the loss of the earlier entries' realism, most would agree that the change of direction has been a big part of the franchise's success, with the switch from car-focused crime movies to vehicular heist movies being hailed as a particularly clever move.

articles.title: The Sweet Change Patrick Stewart Brought To His Star Trek Show After William Shatner’s Era
articles.summary: He had a novel idea that changed Trek forever.
articles.content:
Patrick Stewart's death has brought a litany of stories about the late actor , and many of those have been about his time starring on Star Trek: The Next Generation . It goes without saying that Stewart remains beloved for playing one of Trek' s best characters . On top of that, though he also brought about a sweet change to the show that wasn't even present amid William Shatner 's tenure on within the franchise.

While William Shatner's era of Star Trek resulted in some big feuds between its cast , that wasn't the case with The Next Generation . They all remained good friends for decades, and that lovely fact made the late Jean-Luc Picard star's death all the more devastating. It was both heartwarming and upsetting to see the cast share their tributes and memories of Stewart , given they were struggling with the loss of a good friend.

While Patrick Stewart 's death was hard to fathom, at least he and his former Star Trek castmates got to work together one more time in Season 3 of Picard much to fans' delight. It's still wild to think that Stewart passed just a few years after the finale aired, and with that in mind, we're truly lucky to have witnessed that sequel series.

articles.title: Emma Frost's Darkest Secrets Are Coming Back to Haunt Her, and the X-Men May Never Recover
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Emma Frost's past is coming back to haunt her, and this time it wasn't even her fault, although she has blamed herself for years. When she debuted in Marvel Comics, Emma Frost was a villain working with the Hellfire Club, but over time, her past was revealed, and it was shown that she was someone […]
articles.content:
In X-Men United #9 by Eve L. Ewing, Evan Narcisse, and Ruairi Coleman, the story opens many years earlier at the Massachusetts Academy when Emma was training her teenage mutant team known as the Hellions . However, what happened next showed that one of the most horrific incidents in Emma's history was caused by someone else entirely.

This issue showed a training exercise with the Hellions sparring, and when things got a little dangerous, Emma proved that she wasn't anything like Professor X, and she believed in the survival of the fittest. The Hellions were the teenage mutants Emma was teaching, direct rivals to the New Mutants at Xavier's Institute. However, they were not long for this world, and their deaths caused Emma to go to Professor X and admit that his ways were better than her own. This issue showed Emma confronting someone in her bedroom.

This was Justina LaGuardia, and she is a powerful mutant. She debuted in Giant-Size X-Men #1 (2025), and Professor X tried to recruit her, but she rejected him. She then erased his memory of their meeting, which shows how powerful she really is. Her power is mimicking other mutants' powers. Erasing Professor X's memory using his own powers was impressive. She made her return in X-Men United #7 when it was revealed she was responsible for the kidnapping of Blade's daughter, and she proved powerful enough to take out Blade's father when all was said and done.

Here she did it again when she erased Emma Frost's memories of meeting her. But not before she programmed Emma to do something that the Hellions' leader would long regret. It turns out that Justina was working behind the scenes many years before. She told Emma that she was the “most superior of Homo sapiens superior.” She then told Emma to call the X-Men, offer a truce, and invite them over for dinner. She said Emma wouldn't remember anything, and then Emma would blame the X-Men for what happened next.

This story took place in Uncanny X-Men #281 (1991) by Jim Lee, Whilce Portacio, and John Byrne, and it was the storyline where almost all the Hellions died. Emma did, in fact, invite the X-Men over for dinner, offering a truce. However, tempers flared, and the two sides began to fight. The worst was yet to come when Trevor Fitzroy and his Upstarts attacked. Fitzroy released futuristic Sentinels, and he slaughtered several Hellions before striking down Emma Frost and seeming to kill Jean Grey. Emma ended up in a coma, and eventually this led to her redemption. This new comic reveals that Justina was responsible for everything that happened that night.

If Uncanny X-Men #281 was the road to Emma Frost's redemption, X-Men United #9 might be leading to her downfall. Emma was not responsible for what happened that fateful night with the X-Men and Hellions, but if these memories are unlocked, there is no telling what that could do to her mind. With Justina back, it is clear that she is once again manipulating Emma, and it is unclear what her overall plans are. However, it has already caused a fracture in this X-Men team thanks to something that happened earlier this year.

In the one-shot comic, X-Men: The Hellfire Murder , Sebastian Shaw had invited mutants to the annual party , but he had an ominous plan. He intended to depower all mutants who were not willing to follow him, and he had his own deadly plans. When Shaw was found dead, Wolverine and Jubilee began to investigate, and Wolverine believed the Brotherhood did it when he found Mystique, Destiny, Empath, Mastermind, and Toad together. He realized they planned to kill Shaw but failed, and he decided he would let them go and not reveal anything he knew to keep the peace.

Then the twist at the end of the issue revealed who really killed Sebastian Shaw. Wolverine met up with Emma Frost at a bar and said that he knew she killed Shaw. She had an alibi because she was with Namor when it happened, but she is a powerful telepath and did it anyway. However, Wolverine agreed to keep her secret because Shaw was better off dead, given what he was planning to do.

This issue had Emma slip up after her memories began to get fuzzy. The X-Men told her they saw a hellish version of her on an earlier mission who accused them of betrayals against mutantkind. Wolverine told her that everyone knows he had blood on his hands, and Emma was hiding something. When Emma mentioned her “subtleties,” Kitty Pryde put two and two together and realized Emma was the one who killed Sebastian Shaw. Emma admitted it, but this put the X-Men in a state of unease. When Iceman said they couldn't trust her anymore, she left, and when they went to get more information from Wolverine, he had left too. Emma's past is coming back to haunt her, and the X-Men are losing trust in each other.

What are your thoughts on Emma Frost and her long relationship with the X-Men? Let us know how you think this storyline is going to conclude in the comments below.

Starring in four major movies just this year, Robert Pattinson 's star power has been put to the test, and even Ben Affleck is noticing.

After seeing Christopher Nolan's " The Odyssey " for the first time, the actor consulted his close friend and star of the film, Matt Damon, to discuss Pattinson's performance as Antinous, the antagonistic ringleader of Penelope's suitors.

"Ben Affleck probably talked to me for 20 minutes about just Rob after he saw the movie," Damon said during a screening event for the film at the David Geffen Theater in the Academy Museum on Saturday night (via EW ). "When they talk about a brave performance — Ben goes, ‘You had the benefit of all of the might and power of Christopher Nolan storytelling at your back' and I went, ‘Yeah.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Russell Crowe Sci-Fi Thriller 'Bluefly' Adds 'Beast' Star Daniel MacPherson (EXCLUSIVE)

articles.title: Some Of The Olsen Twins’ Iconic Movies Are Finally Streaming, But I’m Still Hoping Another Film Gets Added
articles.summary: Brb, I'm gonna make popcorn!
articles.content:
Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen may be best known for their shared role as Michelle Tanner on Full House , but the child actors -- who eventually left Hollywood -- also launched their own cinematic universe of sorts. In the '90s and early 2000s, the duo starred in several TV and direct-to-video movies. For the longest time, most of these movies were only available to fans who owned the hard copies, but that’s starting to change as a handful of their movies have popped up on Prime Video (though one of my favorite titles hasn't been added).

As of writing this, eight Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen movies are currently available to stream for Prime Video subscription holders. Four of them are from the early days of the twins’ career and were filmed while Full House was still airing new seasons. The titles include To Grandmother’s House We Go , a Christmas movie and the first of their television films; the Halloween flick Double Double Toil and Trouble ; It Takes Two , a loose book-to-screen adaptation of Mark Twain’s The Prince and the Pauper; and How the West Was Fun .

While the rest of us were being "normal kids," the Olsen twins were busy producing and starring in a total of fourteen movies between 1992 and 2004. Eight films aren't a bad start, but there are still a lot that need to be added to complete the Mary-Kate and Ashley Cinematic Universe. However, there is one movie that I need to be added ASAP: the 2001 flick Holiday in the Sun .

As bummed as I and several other Olsen twin fans are that Holiday in the Sun isn’t one of the eight featured on Prime Video (as of now), it doesn’t put too much of a damper on the reveal. After all, we’ve waited years for even one of their films to hit streaming services, and now we have access to half their filmography.

I guess it’s time for me to pause my marathon of watching all the new and upcoming Christmas movies and head over to Prime Video to revisit some of these gems. Maybe if enough of us watch, the streamer will add Holiday in the Sun or any of the other Olsen twins movies!

articles.title: Major Shonen Jump Anime Confirms Season 2 Return After Manga Finale (First Look Revealed)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha A major Shonen Jump series has officially released its final chapter after five years, and now it's confirmed the anime's return for its second season after the manga's grand finale. Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch first announced it was going to be ending with its final chapter last week, and now that's indeed come to pass […]
articles.content:
Witch Watch wrapped up the TV anime's debut season last year after a successful first outing. It was such a hit that the franchise quickly confirmed that Season 2 would be in the works, but not much had been revealed about the new season at the time. But with the end of the manga this week, Witch Watch Season 2 has released its first look as it gears up for its debut next year. You can check it out below.

Now that Witch Watch has officially ended with Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine after a five year run , Witch Watch has confirmed that Season 2 of the anime will be making its debut on screens sometime next year. No release date or window has been announced as of this time, nor have any details about potential returning production staff or cast neither. It's still a rather mysterious production, but with a 2027 return set it won't be too much longer before the anime starts to reveal more about what to expect from its return.

Witch Watch' s debut season was directed by Hiroshi Ikehata and Masao Kawase for Bibury Animation Studios with Deko Akao handling the scripts, Haruko Iizuka handling the character designs, Mutsumi Takemiya editing the anime, and Yukari Hashimoto composing the music. There's a hope that the production staff will be returning for their respective roles given how well received that first season was last year , but the voice cast is ready for their new season coming our way.

“Congratulations on the completion of the original work!” Nico voice star Rina Kawaguchi stated in a special message to Witch Watch creator Kenta Shinohara on the anime's official website . “Thank you for the wonderful story! I truly love both the comedic episodes, which are full of Shinohara-sensei's signature style and make viewers happy, and the serious episodes that really tighten things up.” But although the star is saying goodbye to the series, there's a hope she returns in the anime's future.

If you wanted to catch up on Witch Watch ahead of the second season, you can now find its episodes now streaming with platforms such as Netflix, Hulu and Hulu on Disney+, Crunchyroll and more in the meantime with both Japanese and English language audio. You can also check out the manga's final chapter completely for free with Shueisha's MangaPlus service or Viz Media's digital Shonen Jump library. And given its wacky adventures and intense action, you're going to want to.

Are you excited to see Witch Watch return for a new season? What are you hoping to see from the new episodes? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda Insider Gives New Update on Majora's Mask Remake
articles.summary: A Nintendo insider has given a new update on the rumored remake of The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask. Before Breath of the Wild came along, Majora's Mask was commonly viewed as the second greatest Legend of Zelda game of all time, behind only Ocarina of Time. Now its placement is more debatable, but it's […]
articles.content:
The new update comes from Nash Weedle , an insider known for scoops pertaining to Nintendo, who, among other things, was one of the first to relay word of the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Recent reports , including from the reliable Nate the Hate , have suggested that a remake of Majora's Mask is not only not in the works, but not in the immediate plans of Nintendo. Nash Weedle's new update seems to suggest otherwise.

According to Nash Weedle, translated by Hugo Gaming , the remake is real, or at least he believes it is, based on one single piece of information provided to him. He does not disclose what this piece of information is, though.

“I’ve received some information about this supposed remake,” said Nash Weedle. “For now, I can only tell you that I’m looking into it. But I assure you that this one piece of information alone has made me believe that the Majora’s Mask remake is real.”

Let's take this new report at face value and also assume that development on The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask Remake has already begun or is imminent. It took three years for Nintendo to remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . For various reasons, Majora's Mask should be quicker than this, but at the bare minimum it won't take longer. So, if a remake of Majora's Mask has begun or is about to begin, we are looking at a late 2028 release date at the earliest, but 2029 and 2030 are certainly on the table as well.

The question is when it will begin. The team that would work on it is no doubt going to support Ocarina of Time , but this doesn't take the full team. Meanwhile, the holiday is imminent, so perhaps development will begin at the start of 2027, but this is just speculation. The game needs minimal time in pre-production, considering it's both a remake and going to be in the same style and spirit as the Ocarina of Time Remake , presumably. In other words, less to figure out in pre-production.

At the moment of publishing, Nintendo has not been drawn out for comment. We do not expect this to change, but if it does, we will update the story accordingly.
